chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ayman ibn Muhraz, from Abu Asama Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not withhold anything from a beggar at all; if he had something, he would give it, or else he would say: 'Allah will bring it.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) respond when he had no material wealth to give a beggar?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) consistent practice of never repelling a beggar, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social responsibility and the spiritual merit of charity. It illustrates that even when material wealth was lacking, the Prophet’s invocation served as a divine guarantee of provision, reinforcing the concept that Allah is the ultimate source of sustenance (Ar-Razzaq). This narrative is central to the jurisprudence of Zakat and Sadaqah, encouraging believers to emulate the Prophet’s generosity regardless of their immediate financial capacity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Ayman Bin Muhraz, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not forbid a beggar at all! If there was (something) with him<sup>saww</sup>, he<sup>saww</sup> would give it, or else he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Come with it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Isma‘il ibn Mehran from Ayman ibn Muhriz from abu Usamah, Zayd al-Shahham who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
never denied someone asking for help. If he had something with him, he gave charity; if not, he would say, ‘May Allah give you (charity).”’
